Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a challenging and overwhelming experience, and it's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time. As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas of support that might be helpful to you.

The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it can provide us with valuable insights into your emotional well-being during the postpartum period. Please know that everything we discuss today is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings.

We'll be going through 10 questions together, and I'll ask them in a way that feels conversational and natural. Your responses will help me understand your experiences and emotions over the past week. Don't worry about answering "correctly" or "incorrectly" - I just want to hear your honest thoughts and feelings.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that you're not alone in this journey, and it's okay to ask for help. Many new mothers experience emotional challenges during the postpartum period, and seeking support is a sign of strength, not weakness.

Let's get started with the first question. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling a bit down or unhappy?

Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, taking care of the baby is a lot of work, and I'm just exhausted. I used to love reading and going for walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or interest in doing those things. Even simple tasks like showering and getting dressed feel like a huge effort. I've been feeling really down and unhappy, and it's hard to explain why. I just feel like I'm not doing a good job as a mom, and that's really getting to me. I worry all the time about the baby's health and safety, and it's hard to calm myself down when I start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm doing everything I need to do, but I'm not really enjoying any of it. And that's not like me at all. I used to be a happy person, but now I just feel sad and discouraged a lot of the time. (pausing, getting a bit tearful) Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, taking care of the baby is my main priority, and it's been really overwhelming. I used to love planning outings or trying new things, but now I just feel too tired and anxious to even think about it. Sometimes I'll make plans with my partner or friends, but then I'll get really worried about how the baby will do without me, or if I'm doing enough for them, and it just feels like too much. I've been having trouble sleeping and I'm always exhausted, so it's hard to muster up the energy to look forward to things. Even simple tasks, like taking a shower or getting dressed, feel like a huge effort. I've been feeling really down and discouraged a lot of the time, and it's hard to find the motivation to do things I used to enjoy. I just feel like I'm not doing a good job as a mom, and that's really getting to me. I worry all the time about the baby's health and safety, and it's hard to calm myself down when I start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. (pausing, getting a bit tearful) Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's definitely been happening to me. I feel like I'm constantly blaming myself for everything that goes wrong with the baby. If they're crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If they're not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If they're not eating enough, I think it's because I'm not producing enough milk. It's like, no matter what happens, I always find a way to blame myself. And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. If the house is a mess, I think it's because I'm a terrible mother and can't even take care of my own home. If my partner is stressed, I think it's because I'm not supporting them enough. It's like, I'm just constantly feeling guilty and inadequate, and it's really hard to shake that feeling. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and I'll just start crying because I feel like I'm not doing a good enough job. I feel like I'm just winging it all the time, and that I'm just waiting for something to go terribly wrong because of my own failures as a mother. (starting to tear up) It's just really hard to not blame myself all the time...
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... I've been feeling that way a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or rocking them to sleep, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if the baby stops breathing? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate their development? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm on edge all the time. Even when everything is fine, and the baby is healthy and happy, I still can't shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby on my own when my partner goes back to work. I'll worry about everything, really. (laughs nervously) I've even caught myself worrying about things that are completely out of my control, like what if there's a power outage and the baby's monitor doesn't work? Or what if there's a fire in the house and we can't get out in time? It's just... my mind is always going, always racing with these worst-case scenarios, and it's exhausting. (sighs) I feel like I'm just constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's hard to calm myself down, even when my partner tries to reassure me that everything is okay. I just feel like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? (looks down, fidgeting with hands)
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding) Yes... that's happened to me a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, just going about my day, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my breath will get short, and I'll just feel like I'm frozen in fear. It's like, my mind will just start racing with all these terrible thoughts, and I'll feel like I'm completely out of control. Sometimes it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just seems to come out of nowhere. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I've had moments where I'm just holding the baby, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear that something is going to happen to them. Or I'll be walking down the stairs with the baby, and I'll suddenly feel like I'm going to trip and fall. It's like, my mind is just constantly catastrophizing, and it's really hard to shake the feeling of fear and panic. (looks down, her voice shaking slightly) Sometimes I'll even feel like I'm having a heart attack or something, my heart will be racing so fast. It's just... it's really scary, and it's hard to know how to make it stop. (pauses, taking another deep breath) I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but even they don't always understand what's going on. They'll just tell me to calm down, or that everything is okay, but it's hard to calm down when you're feeling that level of fear and panic. (looks up, tears in her eyes) It's just really hard to deal with, you know.

I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(sighs) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. Even when the baby is sleeping, I'll lie awake at night feeling anxious and overwhelmed. My mind just starts racing with all these thoughts and worries, and I feel like I'm stuck in this never-ending cycle of stress and anxiety. I'll think about everything that's going wrong, and everything that could go wrong, and it just feels like it's all piling up on top of me. (pauses, rubbing her eyes) I've been feeling really unhappy and overwhelmed, and it's hard to shake that feeling, even when I'm trying to relax. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed, and I'll just start crying because I feel so overwhelmed and unsure of how to make everything okay. (looks down, her voice shaking slightly) It's like, I'm just feeling so much pressure to be a good mom, and to take care of everything, and it's just feeling really overwhelming. And the lack of sleep isn't helping, of course. I'm just feeling really exhausted and drained all the time, and it's hard to know how to make it stop. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I just feel like I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in her eyes) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I should be happy, right? I have a beautiful baby, a loving partner, a comfortable home... but despite all of that, I just can't shake this feeling of sadness and emptiness. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything. I'm not feeling the joy, the excitement, the love... I'm just feeling numb, and sad, and overwhelmed. (pauses, wiping away a tear) Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I feel so sad and miserable. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, all the things I'm failing at, and it just feels like too much to bear. (sighs) I've been feeling really discouraged, too. Like, I'll try to do something, and it won't work out, and I'll just feel like I'm a failure. And that feeling of failure just snowballs, and it's hard to stop it. (looks down, her voice shaking) I just feel like I'm not good enough, like I'm not cut out for this whole mom thing. And that's a really hard feeling to deal with, because I want to be a good mom, I want to be happy, I want to enjoy this time with my baby... but it's just not happening right now. (pauses, taking a deep breath) Sorry, I'm just really struggling with this.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down her face) Yes... that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be going about my day, and then suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming wave of sadness and emotion, and I'll start crying. Sometimes it's because of something specific, like the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe them, or my partner is stressed and I feel like I'm not supporting them enough. But other times, it's just... I don't know, it's like everything just feels too much, and I'll just start crying. (sobs) I've been feeling so overwhelmed and anxious, and it's like my emotions are just right at the surface all the time. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing their diaper, or just sitting there holding them, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm just so grateful to have this little person in my life, but at the same time, I'm just so scared and unsure of how to take care of them. (cries some more) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the toast will burn, and I'll just start crying because it feels like everything is just too much. (laughs through tears) I know it sounds silly, but it's just... I don't know, it's like I'm just so raw and emotional all the time, and everything just feels like too much to handle. (wipes away tears with a tissue) Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now.
